title: Muffin — Pipeline
description: Is the ingestion actually working? Backlog depth, run outcomes and what each run did. Everything here comes from market.refresh_run / backlog_sample, which are SAMPLES — the live pending_* views cost ~8.4s to count (pending_prices alone is 5.4s, over the 8s statement timeout), so no panel may query them directly.

panels.title: Total work outstanding
panels.description: Every backlog added together. The shape is the question: a line that descends is draining, a flat line with successful runs underneath it is the stall this system has hit five times.

targets.rawSql:
select sampled_at as time, sum(depth) as "all backlogs"
  from market.backlog_sample
 where $__timeFilter(sampled_at) and error is null
 group by sampled_at order by sampled_at

panels.title: Backlog depth by resource
panels.description: Per backlog. A FLAT line here while the matching resource reports ok is the signature to recognise — see the 'backlog is not draining' alert.

targets.rawSql:
select sampled_at as time, backlog as metric, depth as value
  from market.backlog_sample
 where $__timeFilter(sampled_at) and error is null and depth > 0
 order by sampled_at

panels.title: Backlogs that could not be counted
panels.description: NULL depth is NOT zero. A view that has started timing out would read as drained if its failure were recorded as an empty result — the same confusion between 'refused' and 'has nothing' that this pipeline has hit six times. Anything appearing here needs looking at.

targets.rawSql:
select sampled_at as time, backlog as metric, duration_ms as value
  from market.backlog_sample
 where $__timeFilter(sampled_at) and error is not null
 order by sampled_at

panels.title: Run outcomes
panels.description: `skipped` is a SUCCESS — the TTL guard found the data fresh. But a resource that ONLY ever skips is not working, which is why the two are separate series rather than one 'ok'.

targets.rawSql:
select date_trunc('hour', started_at) as time,
       case when not ok then 'failed' when skipped then 'skipped' else 'ran' end as metric,
       count(*) as value
  from market.refresh_run
 where $__timeFilter(started_at)
 group by 1, 2 order by 1

panels.title: Rows written per resource
panels.description: Throughput — but read it beside the backlog panel. A `written` that looks healthy while the backlog is flat means the page is not advancing: derive_security_metrics returned 'written: 7386' twice, byte-identical, doing the same work forever.

targets.rawSql:
select date_trunc('hour', started_at) as time, resource as metric, sum(written) as value
  from market.refresh_run
 where $__timeFilter(started_at) and written > 0
 group by 1, 2 order by 1

panels.title: Time since each resource last succeeded
panels.description: The warm-up runs every 3 hours, so anything over 12 is four consecutive misses.

targets.rawSql:
select resource,
       round(extract(epoch from (now() - max(finished_at) filter (where ok))) / 3600.0, 1)
         as "hours since ok",
       max(finished_at) filter (where ok) as "last success"
  from market.refresh_run
 where started_at > now() - interval '30 days'
 group by resource
 order by 2 desc nulls first

panels.title: Recent failures
panels.description: The reason, not just the fact. Since 2026-08-13 an application failure answers 200 with `ok:false`; a bare 502 with no body means the WORKER died — look at memory, not at error handling.

targets.rawSql:
select started_at as "when", resource, http_status as "http", left(error, 160) as error
  from market.refresh_run
 where $__timeFilter(started_at) and not ok
 order by started_at desc limit 100
